user.text: When navigating from the dashboard to a project, I want the project's title to appear instantly, but I don't want to prefetch the rest of the project page.

history.assistant:
The project title should now show up right away when you click a project on the dashboard, and the rest of the page is no longer prefetched. `npx next build` passed with exit code 0, but I haven't checked it in a browser. Next.js only prefetches in production, so you'd need `next start` to see it.

Here's what changed:

- **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`:**
  - Added `export const prefetch = 'partial'`, which turns on partial prefetching for this route only.
  - Split the page into two parts, each with its own loading fallback:
    - `ProjectTitle` reads the slug and calls the cached `getProjectTitle`. It gets fetched before you click, so it's ready immediately.
    - `ProjectDetails` starts with `await navigation()`. That keeps the description and activity (the slow 800 ms `getProjectDetails`) out of every prefetch. They load only after you click, showing "Loading details..." until then, and they're still cached.
- **`app/page.tsx`:** the dashboard links now use `prefetch={true}`. A normal link only prefetches the part of the page that's the same for every project, and the title depends on the slug. This setting makes each link also fetch its own project's title ahead of time.

One thing to watch: each visible link with `prefetch={true}` sends a request to the server. That's fine for a short list like this one. For a long list, the Next.js docs suggest prefetching when the user hovers instead.

The build also edited `tsconfig.json` itself: it set `jsx` to `react-jsx` and added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`.
